elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Retained in 15.2(a)(i): "Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of Sanofi". Sanofi is Customer; the no-consent affiliate right is preserved unaltered by the redline.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Rewritten 15.2(a)(ii) first prong: "Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement in whole to its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser ... in connection with the sale of all or substantially all of its assets to which this Agreement relates, or in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction." All three trigger events (merger, acquisition, substantially-all-assets sale) survive the split.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Chapeau 15.2(a) bars assignment "without the consent of the other Party, except as follows", and both retained exceptions for RevMed are now consent-gated: affiliate assignment "with the consent of Sanofi" (i) and Change of Control successor assignment "with the consent of Sanofi" (ii). No residual no-consent path for RevMed remains.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: 15.2(a)(i) retains "(not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned)" and the new 15.2(a)(ii) RevMed prong adds "(not to be unreasonably withheld)". Every operative RevMed assignment permission carries the reasonableness standard; the chapeau's bare consent for unenumerated assignments is pre-existing and outside the element.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "In no event shall RevMed assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder to a competitor of Sanofi." Unconditional and covers rights/obligations as well as the whole Agreement, so the Change of Control acquirer route cannot be used to reach a Sanofi competitor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3(c) enumerates RevMed's termination grounds exhaustively as 12.2(b) material breach, 12.2(c) insolvency, 12.2(d) Sanofi Competing Product and 12.2(e) cessation — none keyed to a Sanofi Change of Control; the only CoC-based termination is Sanofi's own right under 12.2(a)(ii)A, which runs in our favour and is untouched.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: After the redline only Sanofi may assign to a successor "without consent of RevMed"; RevMed's successor/Change of Control assignment is permitted only "with the consent of Sanofi". That is a consent-gated permission, not the mutual successor right the fallback requires.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Neither prong of 15.2(a)(ii) nor the chapeau imposes any notice obligation; no written-notice mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered clause.
Sanofi's retained no-consent affiliate exception in 15.2(a)(i) is a non-successor assignment permitted without consent, which defeats this element under the ASSIGN fallback rule.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The chapeau consent requirement for assignments outside the enumerated exceptions carries no reasonableness qualifier; the "not to be unreasonably withheld" language appears only in the two RevMed-specific exceptions.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the two Customer-side carve-outs are retained verbatim, RevMed's previously unconditional Change of Control assignment is now consent-gated with a reasonableness standard, an express competitor bar is added, and no Vendor termination right attaches to a Sanofi Change of Control.

The fallback is deliberately not reached (successor assignment is not mutual and unconditional, no written-notice mechanic, and Sanofi's no-consent affiliate exception defeats "other assignments require consent"), which is acceptable because completion at the preferred level suffices and the fallback would surrender Sanofi's no-consent affiliate right.

Minimal: the only structural change is splitting the former "Either Party may, without consent" sentence into party-specific prongs so the consent gate can attach to RevMed alone; Sanofi's prong, the affiliate prong and the chapeau are unchanged, and the single added sentence is required by the competitor-bar element. No survival tails, notice procedures, expense language or other extras were introduced.

Preserves intent: the Change of Control definition, Sanofi's 12.2(a)(ii)A termination right and the Section 12.3(c) effect-of-termination cross-references remain operative and uncontradicted; no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting note (not a defect against the checklist): consider confirming that no other provision (e.g. Competing Product/acquiror mechanics keyed to a RevMed Change of Control) presupposes an unconsented RevMed assignment to its acquirer, so the new consent gate cannot be read as inconsistent with those provisions.
